components.name: Local operator
components.responsibility: Review declared setup mutations and complete host-owned consent and trust actions.
components.process_boundary: Human interaction with the local setup and developer-host surfaces.
components.authority_role: Authority for setup consent and host-owned approvals.
components.multiplicity: One local operator per setup run.
prohibited_authority: Convert setup consent into host trust

components.name: Bicameral public release origin
components.responsibility: Publish immutable macOS and Linux Bot artifacts and exact compatible MCP package coordinates.
components.process_boundary: Public R2 artifact origin, PyPI artifact identity, and GitHub release provenance.
components.authority_role: Authoritative writer of immutable release-binding evidence.
outputs: exact MCP wheel URL and digest
components.multiplicity: One immutable record per released Bot and MCP compatibility tuple.

components.name: Public per-user Bot bootstrap
components.responsibility: Resolve, verify, and install one supported Bot artifact into a user-writable path.
components.deployment_location: Operator process on macOS or Linux.
components.authority_role: Bounded writer of the per-user Bot binary and dashboard assets.
prohibited_authority: Modify a verified binary after verification

components.name: Local Bot CLI developer-host setup controller
components.responsibility: Plan and orchestrate declared terminal package and host steps, reconcile the consented Bicameral-server-scoped host permission grant, and submit verified local evidence to the daemon.
components.authority_role: Bounded orchestrator of explicitly consented local setup mutations.
components.multiplicity: One active setup transaction per operator and host.
prohibited_authority: Write host configuration beyond the consented Bicameral-server-scoped permission entry
Broaden shell, sandbox, network, unrelated MCP server, or host-wide approval settings
Infer activation from prompt text, process presence, or a configured permission grant
Accept setup intent or authority-bearing arguments from a dashboard

components.name: Per-user uv tool installer
components.responsibility: Materialize the exact digest-bound MCP wheel and its Python runtime in dedicated user roots.
components.process_boundary: External uv subprocess invoked with list-form arguments.
components.authority_role: Writer of the bounded MCP package environment.
components.multiplicity: One managed environment per manifest-bound MCP version.

components.name: Released Bicameral MCP package and host adapter
components.responsibility: Serve the thin MCP surface, manage the package-owned hook, and emit and verify durable activation receipts.
components.authority_role: Authoritative writer of managed hook entries and activation receipts.
components.multiplicity: One package installation with independent adapter state per host.
prohibited_authority: Grant host trust or broad tool permissions

components.name: Claude Code or Codex developer host
components.responsibility: Persist MCP registration, own workspace and hook trust, apply tool approvals, and emit genuine SessionStart events.
components.process_boundary: Released host process and user configuration.
components.repository_runtime: External Claude Code or Codex distribution.
components.authority_role: Authoritative writer of host registration and trust state.
components.multiplicity: Zero or one installation per supported host id; hosts remain independent.
prohibited_authority: Claim Bicameral activation without a verified receipt
Reuse one host's trust for another host

components.name: Local Bicameral daemon
components.responsibility: Serve ToolRequest responses and exclusively reduce, persist, invalidate, and project operator-local capability readiness.
components.authority_role: Authoritative writer of operator-local capability readiness and Product authority for ToolRequest responses.
components.multiplicity: One active daemon per operator product home.
prohibited_authority: Mutate host MCP or hook configuration
Treat setup receipts as canonical Decision state
Bind readiness to a bridge session, pairing request, or Product
Accept dashboard setup, validation, repair, uninstall, receipt, executable, or provider control

components.name: Hosted or loopback dashboard readiness surface
components.responsibility: Render an authorized daemon readiness projection, copy safe terminal guidance, and navigate explicitly to Product discovery.
components.process_boundary: Browser surface using the loopback API or an already-authorized hosted bridge read.
components.multiplicity: Zero or more browser sessions; none is required for readiness to exist.
prohibited_authority: Invoke setup, validation, repair, or uninstall
Write readiness or submit setup receipts
Select an executable, developer host, or reasoning provider
Supply pairing tokens, Product identifiers, local paths, or shell fragments to setup
Create, join, select, register, bind, or open a Product as a side effect

components.name: Operator per-user filesystem
components.responsibility: Persist bounded product binaries, package environment, host configuration, sanitized receipts, and readiness records.
components.authority_role: Persistence owner only; authority remains with each declared writer.
components.multiplicity: One filesystem boundary per operating-system user.
prohibited_authority: Turn file presence into activation proof

relationships.interaction: Provides the exact Bot artifact, manifest, and integrity evidence.
relationships.medium: HTTPS from the public versioned artifact origin.
authority_boundaries: A floating latest pointer resolves to an immutable version before installation.
Release evidence does not authorize host mutation.

relationships.interaction: Provides exact compatible MCP wheel and descriptor coordinates.
authority_boundaries: A manifest without an MCP binding cannot start package setup.
Hand-entered package coordinates are invalid.

relationships.interaction: Reviews and confirms the exact setup plan.
relationships.handoff: Foreground consent scoped to the displayed mutation set.
authority_boundaries: Setup consent is not workspace, hook, or tool trust.
Declining consent causes no mutation.

relationships.interaction: Installs or removes the exact MCP wheel in dedicated per-user roots.
relationships.medium: Direct list-form subprocess invocation without a shell.
relationships.handoff: Exit status plus independently verified package metadata.
payloads: direct wheel URL with SHA-256 fragment
authority_boundaries: No ambient PATH executable satisfies provenance.
No global Python environment may be mutated.

relationships.interaction: Registers, inspects, or removes the user-scoped Bicameral MCP server through the official host CLI.
relationships.handoff: Host-owned persisted registration plus structured or sanitized status.
authority_boundaries: The controller never writes the host MCP config directly.
The host and operator alone own trust.

relationships.interaction: Runs the packaged managed-hook lifecycle and receipt verifier.
relationships.medium: Exact managed executable with fixed list-form arguments and JSON output.
relationships.handoff: Schema-validated adapter status or receipt-verification result.
authority_boundaries: The adapter owns host-document mutation.
The controller does not duplicate the managed command or hook identity.

relationships.interaction: Emits a genuine host-owned SessionStart lifecycle event to the managed adapter.
relationships.handoff: Bounded structured lifecycle input and process-scoped context.
authority_boundaries: Non-managed hooks run only after host-owned trust.
Prompt text, transcripts, credentials, and raw environment are excluded.

relationships.interaction: Performs the ToolRequest capability handshake and bounded preflight.
relationships.handoff: Typed daemon-authored capability and preflight result.
authority_boundaries: MCP does not infer missing daemon capabilities.
Daemon response is Product behavior but the setup receipt is audit evidence.

relationships.interaction: Returns a verified, sanitized, fresh-session activation result.
relationships.handoff: Digest-bound receipt facts without prompt or PTY content.
authority_boundaries: Process sampling and prompt matching cannot replace this handoff.
A receipt for one host cannot activate another.

relationships.interaction: Submits schema-validated local setup evidence for authoritative readiness reduction.
relationships.handoff: Exact package, host, hook, receipt, freshness, and artifact-generation facts.
authority_boundaries: The local CLI proposes verified evidence; only the daemon reduces readiness.
The payload contains no bridge session, pairing request, Product identifier, credential, or caller-supplied shell fragment.

relationships.interaction: Projects daemon-owned capability readiness to an authorized read-only dashboard surface.
relationships.medium: Loopback GET or existing paired hosted-bridge projection GET.
relationships.handoff: DaemonCapabilityReadinessV1 with typed reasons and allowlisted safe terminal guidance.
authority_boundaries: Pairing authorizes only the remote read and is not an input to the readiness reducer.
No setup POST, receipt submission, executable/provider choice, Product identity, token, secret, local path, or shell fragment crosses this relationship.
Copying guidance or navigating to Products changes no daemon state.

states.artifact: Immutable Bot target plus compatible MCP wheel version, URL, SHA-256, release descriptor digest, protocol, and Python requirement.
states.persistence_location: Versioned public release manifest and provenance store.
states.routing_key: Bot release version and target triple.
states.mutation_path: Release CI derives fields from built and published artifacts; records are immutable.
states.lifecycle: Created at release publication and never edited; superseded by a later release.
prohibited_fallbacks: same-origin checksum without release provenance as final authenticity proof

states.artifact: Verified per-user MCP environment with exact package, wheel digest, descriptor, Python runtime, and executable.
states.mutation_path: Direct digest-bound uv tool install, update, or uninstall in dedicated roots.
states.lifecycle: Absent, installed and verified, drifted, or removed.

states.artifact: User-scoped host-native MCP registration for server id bicameral and the absolute managed executable.
states.persistence_location: Claude or Codex user configuration owned by the host.
states.routing_key: host id and MCP server id bicameral.
states.mutation_path: Official claude mcp or codex mcp CLI only.
prohibited_fallbacks: direct config-file write by the daemon

states.artifact: Exactly one package-owned managed SessionStart hook entry with package, executable, command, document, and entry digests.
states.routing_key: host id and stable managed entry identity.
states.mutation_path: Packaged adapter install, update, disable, or uninstall with lock, backup, validation, atomic replace, and re-read.
states.lifecycle: Absent, installed_enabled, installed_disabled, drifted, or removed.
prohibited_fallbacks: direct hook execution as activation proof

states.artifact: Host-owned workspace, hook-definition, and per-tool approval facts.
states.persistence_location: Opaque host-owned trust and permission state.
states.routing_key: host id, workspace identity, and exact hook definition hash.
states.mutation_path: Normal interactive host trust and approval surface only.
states.lifecycle: Unreviewed, accepted or denied by operator, invalidated when the trusted definition changes.
prohibited_fallbacks: managed enterprise policy created by the product

states.artifact: The single Bicameral-server-scoped host permission grant Bicameral added after explicit consent (Claude Code user permission rule mcp__bicameral, or Codex mcp_servers.bicameral.default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"), plus the Bicameral-owned record of exactly which rules it added and any prior value.
states.persistence_location: Host user permission file (Claude Code user settings.json or $CODEX_HOME/config.toml [mcp_servers.bicameral] only) and $HOME/.local/share/bicameral/mcp-host-permissions-v1.json.
states.routing_key: host id and the exact Bicameral-owned rule set.
states.mutation_path: Consented setup or repair applies the minimum scoped change with backup and atomic replace; repair on correct state is a no-op; uninstall removes only rules Bicameral recorded as its own and never clobbers operator changes.
states.lifecycle: Absent, configured, missing, drifted, or unsupported (registry fallback unavailable).
prohibited_fallbacks: bypassPermissions, defaultMode, or host-wide approval bypass
generic Bash, shell, sandbox, writable-root, or network rules
managed or organization-wide policy as the normal install mechanism
a handwritten tool allowlist that is not derived from the declared registry
weakening an existing stricter deny, ask, or prompt policy
treating a configured grant as activation or readiness

states.artifact: Sanitized durable product receipt binding a genuine fresh SessionStart to the exact host, package, managed hook, daemon protocol, and preflight result.
states.persistence_location: Per-host MCP state directory under the operator home.
states.routing_key: host id, session correlation id, and MCP release descriptor digest.
states.mutation_path: Written once by the managed hook at a genuine fresh-session boundary and verified by the packaged verifier.
states.lifecycle: Created, verified and consumed, expired, or invalidated by binding drift.

states.artifact: Daemon-owned capability readiness enum not_installed, prerequisite_missing, installed_pending_host_action, active_verified, or repair_required with typed reason metadata; v0.1.14 supports only capability_kind mcp.
states.routing_key: operator, capability_kind, subject id, and artifact generation; no bridge, pairing, dashboard-session, or Product key.
states.mutation_path: Daemon-only deterministic reducer over exact release, package, registration, hook, host, and verified receipt facts submitted by local product processes.
states.lifecycle: not_installed -> prerequisite_missing or installed_pending_host_action -> active_verified -> repair_required; repair or uninstall re-enters an earlier state.
prohibited_fallbacks: Product creation, join, selection, registration, binding, or open
dashboard setup, validation, repair, uninstall, or receipt submission

transitions.trigger: Operator starts the supported public Bot bootstrap.
transitions.persistence_effect: A versioned supported target is resolved and verified before the per-user Bot artifact is copied.

transitions.trigger: A verified manifest contains an exact compatible MCP binding and the operator consents.
transitions.persistence_effect: The exact digest-bound MCP wheel is installed in dedicated per-user roots and independently verified.

transitions.trigger: The exact MCP package verifies and the operator selected a supported installed host.
transitions.persistence_effect: The host persists one user-scoped bicameral MCP registration through its official CLI.

transitions.trigger: Host registration verifies and the operator consents to the disclosed managed-hook mutation.
transitions.persistence_effect: The package adapter atomically persists exactly one managed hook while preserving unrelated configuration.

transitions.trigger: The host detects workspace or changed hook definitions requiring review.
transitions.persistence_effect: Only the host records the operator's trust decision for the exact workspace or hook definition.

transitions.trigger: The operator answers the single explicit consent step authorizing Bicameral to configure permissions for the Bicameral MCP server only.
transitions.persistence_effect: The controller adds the broadest host-native Bicameral-server-scoped grant (or, where unavailable, the deterministic read-only allowlist derived from the declared tool registry), records exactly what it added, and leaves every unrelated or stricter host setting untouched. Without consent nothing is written and readiness reports the grant as missing.

transitions.trigger: A trusted normal host starts a fresh session and emits SessionStart.
transitions.persistence_effect: The managed adapter writes one sanitized receipt bound to the exact session, package, configuration, and daemon result.

transitions.trigger: The packaged verifier accepts a fresh activation receipt and all current exact bindings.
transitions.persistence_effect: The local CLI submits verified evidence and the daemon alone records active_verified for only the matching operator, mcp capability, host, and descriptor.

transitions.trigger: Package, registration, managed hook, host trust, daemon protocol, receipt freshness, or release binding no longer matches.
transitions.persistence_effect: Readiness changes to repair_required with a typed reason; stale activation is not reused.

transitions.trigger: The operator confirms the exact reverse-order removal plan.
transitions.persistence_effect: Bicameral-owned host permission grant, managed hook, host registration, MCP environment, receipts, and readiness are removed in order; operator-modified permission entries, unrelated host state, and authentication remain.

scenarios.name: Clean per-user macOS or Linux setup
scenarios.trigger: An operator with a supported host starts setup from a clean user product home.
authority_boundaries: All product mutations are per-user and disclosed before consent.
Host registration uses the host CLI; hook mutation uses the package adapter.
Installation stops pending host action and does not claim activation.
After one explicit consent step the controller configures only the Bicameral-server-scoped host permission; shell, sandbox, network, unrelated MCP, and host-wide approval settings are unchanged.
scenarios.expected_result: Exact package, host registration, and managed hook verify while readiness remains installed_pending_host_action.
scenarios.failure_behavior: The reducer retains independently verified partial facts, emits typed remediation, and never elevates or falls back to a stale package.

scenarios.name: Host-owned trust and durable fresh-session activation
scenarios.trigger: Installation verifies and the operator opens the selected host normally.
authority_boundaries: Only the host records trust.
Only a genuine SessionStart invokes the managed adapter.
Only the packaged verifier can satisfy the activation evidence input.
scenarios.expected_result: The matching host reaches active_verified with a fresh sanitized receipt and exact package/configuration provenance.
scenarios.failure_behavior: Absent, stale, mismatched, or unsanitized evidence leaves readiness pending or repair_required; process and prompt observations do not count.

scenarios.name: Detect and repair exact-binding drift
scenarios.trigger: A package, executable, registration, hook document, host trust hash, protocol, or release binding changes.
authority_boundaries: Repair repeats only mismatched declared steps.
Changed hook definitions always return to host-owned review.
A stale activation receipt is never rebound.
scenarios.expected_result: Repair_required is replaced by active_verified only after exact state and a new fresh-session receipt verify.
scenarios.failure_behavior: Ambiguous or malformed host state fails closed and preserves backups; setup never rewrites it to an empty document.

scenarios.name: Preserving reverse-order uninstall
scenarios.trigger: The operator requests removal and confirms the exact removal plan.
authority_boundaries: Only Bicameral-owned entries and per-user package roots are removed.
Host authentication, session history, unrelated hooks, and unrelated MCP servers remain.
Only the host permission grant Bicameral recorded as its own is removed; a grant the operator changed since setup is preserved and reported.
scenarios.expected_result: The selected host returns to not_installed with preservation evidence and no administrator privilege.
scenarios.failure_behavior: If preservation cannot be proved, removal stops at repair_required and points to the bounded backup.

scenarios.name: Read-only dashboard readiness projection
scenarios.trigger: An authorized loopback or paired dashboard opens Local runtime readiness.
authority_boundaries: Pairing authorizes only the remote read.
The dashboard cannot cause setup, validation, repair, uninstall, or readiness reduction.
Readiness contains no Product identity and Continue to Products is navigation only.
scenarios.expected_result: The dashboard renders the daemon-owned MCP state and may copy bicameral setup mcp without changing daemon or Product state.
scenarios.failure_behavior: Unpaired, revoked, incompatible, or unavailable reads fail visibly while the daemon readiness record remains unchanged.

scenarios.name: Reject dashboard-controlled setup
scenarios.trigger: A dashboard attempts to submit setup intent, a receipt, executable/provider selection, Product identity, or an authority-bearing command argument.
authority_boundaries: The dashboard relationship is projection-only.
The daemon never translates a browser request into a local setup process.
scenarios.expected_result: The request is rejected as an unsupported authority path and no readiness, host, pairing, or Product state changes.
scenarios.failure_behavior: There is no compatibility fallback, queued setup request, hidden shell invocation, or manufactured readiness.
